answer: Forced-Divergence Quorum Sampling works by requiring each identity to answer a random challenge drawn from its own past actions, so a clone farm sharing one history produces identical answers and gets flagged. Honest agents accrue unique voyage logs over time. Each challenge forces a summit of independent checkpoints, and the answer space is a nebula of personal traces. An attacker must run every clone through distinct real interactions, paying full per-identity compute and time costs to fabricate divergence.
